newsitem.title: USA: China 97/98 wheat imports put at 6 mln tonnes-USDA.
newsitem.headline: China 97/98 wheat imports put at 6 mln tonnes-USDA.

text.p: China will likely import six million tonnes of wheat in 1997/98 and four million tonnes in 1996/97, a significant drop from earlier projections, the Agriculture Department chief economist said Monday.

Speaking at USDA's annual Agricultural Outlook Forum, economist Keith Collins said that increasing wheat production in China along with a large increase in stocks, has decreased that nation's need for imported wheat in the short term.
USDA had earlier estimated China's 1997/98 wheat imports at 9.4 million tonnes, and its 1996/97 imports at 7.0 million.
Collins said, however, that looking at the longer term, China will still have "enormous demand" for imported grains.
In response to a question, Collins said that feed grain imports will probably experience the strongest growth in China, due to China's expected increase in livestock production.
